prompt: What actually crosses the network from the storefront to orders so that both join one trace?
hint: It was stored in a database column.

choices.text: The storefront's current span object, serialised in memory
choices.why: Spans are not shipped between services; only ids are.

choices.text: A `traceparent` header
choices.why: Right: four fields, fifty-five characters.

choices.text: A cookie set by Jaeger on the first request of each session
choices.why: Jaeger never sees the requests.

choices.text: Nothing: the Collector matches spans by their timestamps
choices.why: The Collector joins nothing; ids do.

prompt: Match each field of `00-f1523e868eabe70f75294e789580216e-b0844e71b749fd8f-03` to what it is.

pairs.right: The span id of the caller

prompt: The request goes storefront → orders → payments. Which field of `traceparent` is different in the header payments receives from the one orders received?

choices.text: The trace id, so payments can tell the hop apart
choices.why: The trace id never changes along a trace.

choices.text: The parent id
choices.why: Right: it is now the span in orders that made the call.

choices.text: The version, which counts the hops
choices.why: The version is the format's, not a counter.

choices.text: None: the header is forwarded unchanged
choices.why: Then payments would hang its span under the storefront's.

prompt: With `OTEL_PROPAGATORS` unset, the SDK uses `tracecontext,___`.
A company is moving from Zipkin's B3 headers to W3C Trace Context, one service at a time. What keeps traces whole during the move?

choices.text: Converting the old traces stored in the backend overnight, once every service has moved
choices.why: Stored traces are not the problem; live headers are.

choices.text: Turning tracing off until every service is migrated
choices.why: That loses traces for the whole migration.

choices.text: Every service writes both formats until the last old one is gone
choices.why: Right: two propagators in the list.

choices.text: Each service picks the format its own team prefers
choices.why: A mismatched pair breaks the trace at that hop.

prompt: Which operation runs in the service sending a request?

choices.text: Inject
choices.why: Right: it writes the current context into the request.

choices.text: Extract
choices.why: That runs on the receiving side.

choices.text: Export
choices.why: Exporting sends spans to a backend, not context to a service.

choices.text: Sample
choices.why: Sampling decides what is kept, not what travels.

prompt: orders' code never calls inject or extract. How does its trace still connect on both sides?

choices.text: The Collector rewrites its spans with the right parents
choices.why: The Collector does not invent parents.

choices.text: Flask's instrumentation extracts, and `requests`' injects
choices.why: Right. Propagation over HTTP is what automatic instrumentation does best.

choices.text: It shares memory with the storefront through Docker
choices.why: Containers do not share memory like that.

choices.text: It reads the trace id back from the database before every call it makes to another service
choices.why: The column only records the header; nothing reads it to propagate.

prompt: Which of these carriers need inject and extract written by hand, or an instrumentation installed, in the lab? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A message on the RabbitMQ queue
choices.why: Yes: nothing instruments `pika` here.

choices.text: A file dropped for another program to read
choices.why: Yes: no library knows that is a request.

choices.text: An HTTP call from orders to payments
choices.why: The `requests` instrumentation injects it.

choices.text: A row a job will read later
choices.why: Yes, which is why orders stores `traceparent` in one.

prompt: Payments still called `extract`, but the span was started without `context=ctx`. Why did it become the root of a new trace?
hint: What is current at the start of a request?

choices.text: Extract fails when its result is not used
choices.why: It succeeded; the result was just thrown away.

choices.text: The storefront stopped sending the header
choices.why: The storefront was not touched.

choices.text: It started from whatever was current, and nothing was
choices.why: Right. Extracting is not enough; the span must start in what was extracted.

choices.text: Jaeger cannot join spans from a service restarted mid-trace
choices.why: The restart was before the checkout.

prompt: Looking only at the checkout's trace, what is the one clue that payments fell out of it?

choices.text: An error status on orders' `POST` span
choices.why: The call succeeded; nothing is marked.

choices.text: A warning that Jaeger prints at the top of every trace with a missing service
choices.why: Jaeger cannot know a span is missing.

choices.text: A client span with no server span under it
choices.why: Right. The call went out and its other half is in another trace.

choices.text: The trace is shorter in time than the checkout
choices.why: Its root still covers the whole checkout.

prompt: The mailer's spans started 22.8 s after the checkout's. What does that gap measure?

choices.text: How long the message waited in the queue before the mailer took it
choices.why: Right: waiting nobody would see without the trace.

choices.text: How long the e-mail took to send
choices.why: Sending took 20 ms, in its own span.

choices.text: A clock difference between two containers on the same machine
choices.why: One machine has one clock.

choices.text: The time RabbitMQ needed to start
choices.why: RabbitMQ was running throughout.

prompt: Where did the `traceparent` travel on the RabbitMQ message?

choices.text: Inside the JSON body, beside the order
choices.why: The body is only the order.

choices.text: In the message's headers
choices.why: Right, beside the body, like HTTP.

choices.text: In the queue's name, as a suffix
choices.why: The queue is always `orders.placed`.

choices.text: Nowhere: the mailer asks orders for it
choices.why: The mailer never calls orders.

prompt: The messaging conventions would have orders open a `PRODUCER` span around the publish. What would that add to the trace?
hint: What is the mailer's parent today?

choices.text: A second trace for the queue
choices.why: The producer span joins the same trace.

choices.text: The message body, as an attribute
choices.why: Recording the body is not what a producer span is for.

choices.text: The publish as a step of its own, with a duration
choices.why: Right: the consumer's span could hang from it instead of `POST /orders`.

choices.text: Nothing, because RabbitMQ cannot carry headers
choices.why: It carried `traceparent` in the capture.

prompt: The report counted 22 orders and linked to each one's trace. How many spans long was the report's own trace?
Why does the report link to the checkouts instead of making one of them its parent?
hint: How many causes does it have?

choices.text: Jaeger refuses parents from older traces
choices.why: Jaeger has no such rule.

choices.text: 22 causes, and one parent per span
choices.why: Right. Picking one would misrepresent the other 21.

choices.text: Parents only work within one service
choices.why: Parents cross services all the time.

choices.text: Links are faster for the backend to store and to search than a parent is
choices.why: Speed is not why.

prompt: Jaeger stores a link as a reference of type `___`.
Why is it correct that the nightly report's span has no parent?

choices.text: Because its parent was sampled out
choices.why: There was no parent to sample.

choices.text: Nothing called it; a timer did
choices.why: Right. A timer is not a span, so the trace starts at the job.

choices.text: Because jobs are not allowed to have parents in any tracing system
choices.why: A job started by a traced pipeline can and should.

choices.text: Because the report was run by hand in the lab
choices.why: Run by cron it would still have no caller.

prompt: Last night's report never ran. Which signal can tell you?
hint: What exists for work that did not happen?

choices.text: Its trace, which will show an error
choices.why: Work that never ran leaves no trace at all.

choices.text: Its log lines, which will say that it was skipped and give the reason
choices.why: A job that never started writes nothing.

choices.text: A metric of time since the last successful run
choices.why: Right, with an alert when it grows past a day.

choices.text: The links from the checkouts to the report
choices.why: Links come from the report's span, which does not exist.

prompt: To hand context to a child process, OpenTelemetry's convention sets the environment variable ___ in the child.
hint: Same name as the header, in capitals.

prompt: What is baggage?

choices.text: Spans waiting in the batch processor's queue
choices.why: That is the export queue.

choices.text: Pairs that travel with the context
choices.why: Right: keys and values, readable by every service downstream.

choices.text: Attributes copied onto every span automatically by the SDK
choices.why: Baggage is not recorded on spans unless copied.

choices.text: The part of a trace that is too large to export
choices.why: No such thing.

prompt: Which of these may safely go into baggage? Choose all that apply.
hint: It reaches third parties, in plain text.

choices.text: `shop.channel=mobile-app`
choices.why: Yes: means nothing outside the shop.

choices.text: The customer's e-mail address
choices.why: Personal data, sent to every service called.

choices.text: A region, like `south`
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The session token
choices.why: Anyone receiving it could use it.

prompt: The storefront puts `shop.channel` into baggage, and the payments team says their spans do not show it. What is missing?
hint: Baggage travels; it is not recorded.

choices.text: Payments copying it onto its spans, or a processor that does
choices.why: Right. Nothing records baggage on its own.

choices.text: A second `traceparent` header
choices.why: One is enough; this is about baggage.

choices.text: Jaeger's support for baggage, which must be switched on
choices.why: Jaeger only sees what was recorded on spans.

choices.text: An environment variable that tells payments to trust the storefront
choices.why: Trust is not the issue; recording is.

prompt: Put the steps of the trace crossing the queue in order.
hint: From the request to the e-mail.
items: Flask extracts the storefront's `traceparent` in orders
`publish()` injects the current context into the message's headers
The message waits on the queue
The mailer extracts from the headers and starts a `CONSUMER` span
